text: Georg Simmel on the pair: a dyad, 'for its life, it needs both, but for its death, only one.'
Émile Durkheim's first rule in The Rules of Sociological Method (1895) was to treat social facts as things.
In 1892 Albion Small was chosen to found a department of sociology at the new University of Chicago.
Marx never wrote 'false consciousness'. The phrase comes from Engels, in a letter to Franz Mehring of 14 July 1893, ten years after Marx's death.
Ibn Khaldun withdrew for over three years (1375–1378) to Qal'at Ibn Salamah, in what is now Algeria, and came back with a theory of how dynasties rise and fall.
Suicide statistics run late: only 39% of the suicides registered in England and Wales in 2023 had happened that year, because inquests take time.
Across 35 years of research, classroom self-fulfilling prophecies do occur, but they are typically small and more likely to fade than to accumulate.
Erving Goffman spent a year of fieldwork at St Elizabeths Hospital in Washington, which held more than 7,000 patients. The result was Asylums (1961) and the idea of the total institution.
In a study of turn-taking in 10 languages, Japanese speakers replied fastest on average (+7 milliseconds) and Danish speakers slowest (+469).
In 1986 John Laub found boxes of old research files in the basement of Harvard Law School: the Gluecks' records of 500 reform-school boys, which became a landmark study of how people stop offending.
After the London bombings of July 2005, police deployment in central London rose by over 30 per cent for six weeks, and crime there fell relative to outer London.
The Crime Survey for England and Wales put violence in the year to June 2026 at 79 per cent below its 1995 peak.
In 1938 Frank Tannenbaum argued that a young person's first contact with the law can be decisive, an early version of labelling theory.
Ann Oakley brought the sex and gender distinction into British sociology with a 1972 book, written when she was 27.
In 1976 five Black women who worked on the assembly line at General Motors in St Louis sued the company. Their lost case helped inspire Kimberlé Crenshaw's idea of intersectionality.
In an audit study with real employers, childless women received 2.1 times as many callbacks as equally qualified mothers.
The UK gender pay gap for full-time employees was 6.8% in April 2026, down from 16.4% in 2001.
On 5 December 1955, 90 percent of Montgomery's Black citizens stayed off the buses. The one-day boycott became a 13-month campaign.
In Chenoweth and Stephan's data, about 51 percent of nonviolent campaigns succeeded outright, against about 26 percent of violent ones.
Since 2010, fewer than 34 percent of nonviolent campaigns have succeeded, though violent ones did even worse, at 8 percent.
By the end of April 1960, over 50,000 students had taken part in the lunch-counter sit-ins that began in Greensboro.
William Gamson followed 53 American challenging groups: 31 of them (58 percent) gained new advantages or acceptance.
In one of Stanley Milgram's first small-world trials, just 3 of the 60 folders arrived, after passing through an average of 8 people.
In 2011 the whole Facebook network of about 721 million active users had an average distance of 4.74 steps between any two people.
The friendship paradox: in the 2011 Facebook graph, 92.7% of users had fewer friends than their friends had on average.
The Swedish Tax Authority restructured its offices to stay within a 150-person limit, inspired by Dunbar's number.
The first US census, in 1790, had only three racial categories: free whites, all other free persons and slaves.
The first critical race theory conference was held in Madison, Wisconsin, in 1989.
Pettigrew and Tropp's 2006 meta-analysis of 713 samples from 515 studies found that contact between groups typically reduces prejudice.
Field experiments in the US since 1989 find that white applicants receive on average 36% more callbacks than equally qualified African Americans.
By tradition Michael Young coined 'meritocracy' for his 1958 satire, which warned against it. The word had in fact appeared two years earlier.
From 1980 to 2016 the global top 1% captured 27% of total income growth.
A famous estimate said that if people married at random, US household income inequality would fall sharply. A 2015 correction shrank the effect almost to nothing: a Gini of 0.430 to 0.420.
